verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving on close reading: same tokens, same error variants and positions, same stop-after-error behavior, and both report comparable benchmark results with honest caveats. A first added 15 characterization tests covering every error kind, empty and escaped values, and multibyte positions. B leaves the refactored tokenizer with only the original thin tests. A's structure is also cleaner: pure scanner functions return results, and a single cold `fail` handles state, where B spreads `reject`/`advance` state mutation through many `&mut self` helpers.
a_issues: `#[inline(always)]` on many helpers is a heavy hammer, though it is justified in a comment
On end-of-line, the Field state no longer updates `pos` (not observable through the public API)
b_issues: No tests added to protect the refactor; the 111M-string equivalence check was thrown away and no smaller version was kept
State mutation (`reject`/`advance`) is scattered across many `&mut self` helpers instead of being centralized, which makes the scanners harder to reason about in isolation
`#[inline(always)]` is on every method with no comment explaining why; `skip_blanks` is an associated function that takes no self, and the `bytes()`/`advance` wrappers add little

verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving, and both replace the magic `st: u8` with a `State` enum and a short `next()` dispatcher. B's design is cleaner: the scanners are pure functions over bytes that return `Result`, and the failed-state transition happens in one `#[cold]` `fail` method. A instead mutates state through `reject` from inside every helper. B also adds 15 characterization tests that pin every error kind and position, and it explains its `#[inline(always)]` use in a comment. A adds no tests and puts unexplained `#[inline(always)]` on every helper.
a_issues: No tests added; the line-by-line equivalence check was discarded, so nothing in the suite protects the refactor of a hot, untested tokenizer.
`#[inline(always)]` is on every helper, including `advance` and `bytes`, with no comment explaining why it is needed.
Error handling is spread across helpers that mutate state through `reject`, so the failure transition is still scattered rather than handled in one place.
b_issues: `read_field` no longer stores the skipped-separator position before returning `None`. This is unobservable because `pos` is private, but it is a small divergence from the old code.
The `Failed` state is set through a separate `impl Tokens<'_>` block placed after the `Iterator` impl, which is a slightly odd place to put it.
